Published online:
    September 2, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Canada (North America), with secondary reference to US-Canada trade relations

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES] — references Q2 GDP, 11 months of unchanged rates, prior BoC statements
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES] — December hike priced in, next meeting reassessment flagged
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — ~3 additional hikes penciled in through 2027, sustained oil price risk

Synopsis:
    The Bank of Canada held rates at 2.25% but delivered a notably hawkish pivot. Governor Macklem explicitly signaled willingness to hike multiple times if inflation — currently at 3%, driven by elevated oil prices (~$90/bbl Brent vs. $75 assumed) from the Iran conflict — stays too high. Canada's strong Q2 rebound (3.3% annualized) is complicated by US tariff risks and Canada's retaliatory measures, which add domestic inflationary pressure. Markets now price a December hike and ~3 more in 2026-2027. The BoC also dropped neutral-rate language, reinforcing the hawkish tilt.
